integrity: The seven-vertex witness is verified from its complete exact pair-distance histogram. Sharpness is established by exhaustive enumeration of every labeled simple graph through six vertices, exact connectivity testing, exact shortest-path computation, and exact rational comparison within every fixed-order fixed-size group.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns connected unweighted finite simple graphs and strict ranking reversal at fixed order and fixed edge count. Weak-order equivalence already fails at six vertices because ties under characteristic path length can be split by global efficiency. The seven-vertex statement is an existence result, not a classification of all larger reversing pairs.
title: Seven vertices are the sharp fixed-density reversal boundary for path length and global efficiency
